---
title: "02 — Double pendulum"
---

The canonical two-mode plant used throughout the package: a double pendulum
with modes at 0.6 Hz (Q = 20) and 1.5 Hz (Q = 30) and gain 300. We identify it
the **Pintelon-Schoukens** way, end to end — periodic excitation, leakage-free
measurement, maximum-likelihood fit:

1. **Design** an optimal periodic multisine whose power is split across *both*
   resonances. The Fisher iteration finds the split automatically; the narrower,
   higher-Q mode gets a sharper, taller peak.
2. **Measure** the plant on a digital twin with that drive and take a
   *leakage-free* reference-based FRF (a synchronous, un-windowed DFT averaged
   over whole periods).
3. **Fit** both modes by maximum likelihood, starting from a deliberately
   slightly-off prior.

Before trusting any of it we also look at the **measurement time series** to
confirm the drive is a gentle, low-crest waveform — *coaxing* the suspension,
not slamming it.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots

from system_ident.plant import double_pendulum, SuspensionPlant
from system_ident.model import TFModel
from system_ident.fisher import parameter_covariance
from system_ident.design.pintelon import optimal_excitation
from system_ident.excitation import multisine_from_psd
from system_ident.backends.twin import TwinBackend
from system_ident.loop import SysIDLoop
from system_ident.estimators.gml import GMLEstimator

FS, NPERSEG, N_PERIODS = 32.0, 2048, 8
TOTAL = NPERSEG * N_PERIODS / FS                # 512 s of periodic drive

true  = double_pendulum()                       # canonical two-mode plant
prior = TFModel.from_resonances([(0.55, 14.0), (1.6, 22.0)], gain=250.0)  # slightly off

# Synchronous DFT bin grid: every excited line lands exactly on a bin, so the
# periodic FRF below is leakage-free.
f_all  = np.fft.rfftfreq(NPERSEG, 1 / FS)
band   = (f_all >= 0.1) & (f_all <= 5.0)
freq   = f_all[band]

Pyy    = np.ones_like(freq)
Px_tot = 1.0
Pxx_opt  = optimal_excitation(freq, prior, Pyy, Px_tot, n_iter=6)
Pxx_flat = np.full_like(freq, Px_tot / (freq[-1] - freq[0]))
resp     = np.abs(true.eval(freq))
```

## Optimal drive allocation across two modes

```{python}
#| label: fig-dp-excitation
#| fig-cap: "Two-mode plant: the optimal drive splits power between the 0.6 Hz and 1.5 Hz resonances. The Q=30 mode (1.5 Hz) is narrower, so it receives a sharper, taller peak. Hover to inspect."

T_tot    = 256.0
cov_opt  = parameter_covariance(freq, prior, Pxx_opt,  Pyy, T_tot)
cov_flat = parameter_covariance(freq, prior, Pxx_flat, Pyy, T_tot)
ratio    = np.max(np.diag(cov_flat)) / np.max(np.diag(cov_opt))

SKY  = '#1F8AC0'
GOLD = '#C8973A'
GRAY = '#94A3B8'

fig = make_subplots(
    rows=2, cols=1, shared_xaxes=True,
    subplot_titles=[
        '<b>Plant magnitude</b>  |G(f)| — two modes',
        f'<b>Excitation design</b>  — {ratio:.0f}× variance reduction over flat',
    ],
    vertical_spacing=0.08,
)

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=resp, mode='lines',
    line=dict(color=SKY, width=2.5), name='|G(f)| — double pendulum',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |G| = %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>',
), row=1, col=1)

# Annotate both modes
for f0, label, ax, ay in [(0.6, 'f₁ = 0.6 Hz, Q=20', -65, -35),
                           (1.5, 'f₂ = 1.5 Hz, Q=30',  60, -35)]:
    idx = np.argmin(np.abs(freq - f0))
    fig.add_annotation(
        x=freq[idx], y=resp[idx], xref='x', yref='y',
        text=f'<b>{label}</b>', showarrow=True,
        arrowhead=2, arrowsize=1.1, arrowcolor='rgba(200,151,58,0.75)',
        ax=ax, ay=ay, font=dict(size=10, color=GOLD, family='Outfit, sans-serif'),
        row=1, col=1,
    )

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=np.sqrt(Pxx_opt),
    mode='lines', fill='tozeroy', fillcolor='rgba(200,151,58,0.15)',
    line=dict(color=GOLD, width=2.5), name='Optimal  (Fisher-matched)',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   ASD = %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>',
), row=2, col=1)

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=np.sqrt(Pxx_flat),
    mode='lines', line=dict(color=GRAY, width=1.8, dash='dash'),
    name='Flat  (equal total power)',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   ASD = %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>',
), row=2, col=1)

fig.update_layout(
    template='plotly_white', height=500,
    margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=50, b=55),
    font=dict(family='Outfit, Inter, sans-serif', size=12),
    legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='bottom', y=1.02, xanchor='right', x=1,
                bgcolor='rgba(255,255,255,0.9)', bordercolor='#DCE5F0', borderwidth=1),
)
fig.update_yaxes(title_text='|G(f)|',         type='log', row=1, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig.update_yaxes(title_text='Drive ASD',                  row=2, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig.update_xaxes(title_text='Frequency  [Hz]',            row=2, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig.update_xaxes(gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)',        row=1, col=1)
fig.show()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Why does the 1.5 Hz mode get a sharper peak?

The optimal drive peak width is approximately proportional to the mode's
bandwidth Δf = f₀/Q.  The 1.5 Hz mode has Q = 30, so Δf ≈ 0.05 Hz — narrower
than the 0.6 Hz mode (Q = 20, Δf ≈ 0.03 Hz).  The iteration concentrates power
in a tighter frequency range around the higher-Q mode because that's where its
Jacobian ∂G/∂θ is large.
:::

## Variance numbers

For the plant we are designing against, concentrating the budget on the two
modes buys a large reduction in worst-case parameter variance over spreading the
same power flat across the band:

```{python}
print(f"Flat    — max parameter variance: {np.max(np.diag(cov_flat)):.3e}")
print(f"Optimal — max parameter variance: {np.max(np.diag(cov_opt)):.3e}")
print(f"Variance ratio: {ratio:.1f}×")
```

## Measure the plant — periodic multisine + leakage-free FRF

We hand the optimal allocation to `multisine_from_psd`, which realises it as a
periodic Schroeder multisine (low crest factor, exactly `NPERSEG` samples per
period). The digital twin integrates the true plant; we read the drive monitor
and the mirror response and take the **reference-based, ratio-of-averages** FRF.
Because the drive is periodic, the synchronous DFT is leakage-free — the sharp
resonances are measured without the near-peak bias a windowed random record
would smear in. Only the bins the optimal drive actually excites carry weight.

```{python}
plant = SuspensionPlant({"POS": true}, FS)
tw = TwinBackend(plant, {"C1:EXC": "POS"}, {"C1:RSP": "POS"},
                 fs=FS, sensor_asd=1e-3, seed=0)

drive = multisine_from_psd(Pxx_opt, FS, NPERSEG, N_PERIODS, freq, seed=0)
tw.inject("C1:EXC", drive, FS)
seg = tw.read(["C1:EXC", "C1:RSP"], TOTAL)
mirror = seg["C1:RSP"]

H, H_err, coh = SysIDLoop._estimate_tf_periodic(
    seg["C1:EXC"], seg["C1:RSP"], FS, NPERSEG, band
)
excited = np.isfinite(H_err)
print(f"excited lines: {excited.sum()} / {freq.size}  (all power on the two modes)")
```

## Is the drive gentle? — the measurement time series

The drive is a periodic Schroeder multisine: a smooth, bounded waveform with a
low crest factor, not an impulsive kick. The mirror motion settles into a steady
bounded oscillation — the suspension is being *coaxed*, not slammed.

```{python}
#| label: fig-dp-timeseries
#| fig-cap: "The measurement, first ~64 s. The drive (top) is a smooth low-crest Schroeder multisine; the mirror motion (bottom) is a bounded steady oscillation. Peak drive stays well inside a safe actuator range — coaxing, not slamming."

crest = np.max(np.abs(drive)) / np.std(drive)
t = np.arange(int(64 * FS)) / FS
fig = make_subplots(
    rows=2, cols=1, shared_xaxes=True, vertical_spacing=0.09,
    subplot_titles=[f'<b>Drive</b> — actuator (Schroeder multisine, crest = {crest:.1f})',
                    '<b>Mirror motion</b> — bounded steady oscillation'],
)
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=t, y=drive[:t.size], mode='lines',
              line=dict(color=SKY, width=1.3), name='drive'), row=1, col=1)
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=t, y=mirror[:t.size], mode='lines',
              line=dict(color=GOLD, width=1.5), name='mirror motion'), row=2, col=1)
fig.update_layout(template='plotly_white', height=460,
                  margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=50, b=50),
                  font=dict(family='Outfit, Inter, sans-serif', size=12),
                  legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='bottom', y=1.05, xanchor='right', x=1))
fig.update_yaxes(title_text='drive [cts]', row=1, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig.update_yaxes(title_text='motion [a.u.]', row=2, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig.update_xaxes(title_text='time [s]', row=2, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig.show()
```

## Recover both modes by maximum likelihood

`GMLEstimator` starts from the slightly-off prior and fits the rational model to
the leakage-free FRF and its per-line error bars. Even though the optimal drive
put all its power into two tight clusters, the parametric ML fit reconstructs the
*entire* transfer function — and pins down both resonances.

```{python}
fit = GMLEstimator().fit(freq, H, H_err, prior)

def _modes(model):
    p = np.roots(np.asarray(model.den, float))
    p = p[p.imag > 1e-9]
    out = []
    for pole in sorted(p, key=lambda z: abs(z)):
        w0 = abs(pole)
        out.append((w0 / (2 * np.pi), w0 / (2 * abs(pole.real))))
    return out

print(f"{'mode':>6}   {'true (f0,Q)':>16}   {'prior (f0,Q)':>16}   {'recovered (f0,Q)':>18}")
for i, ((f0t, qt), (f0p, qp), (f0f, qf)) in enumerate(
    zip(_modes(true), _modes(prior), _modes(fit)), start=1):
    print(f"  {i:>4}   ({f0t:.3f} Hz, {qt:4.1f})   ({f0p:.3f} Hz, {qp:4.1f})"
          f"   ({f0f:.3f} Hz, {qf:5.2f})")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-dp-fit
#| fig-cap: "Recovered model (dashed gold) over the true double-pendulum plant (blue), with the leakage-free FRF samples (grey). The optimal drive only excites the two modes — yet the ML fit captures both, and the whole curve in between."

fig2 = go.Figure()
fig2.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=resp, mode='lines',
    line=dict(color=SKY, width=2.5), name='True plant',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |G| = %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>',
))
fig2.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq[excited], y=np.abs(H[excited]), mode='markers',
    marker=dict(color='rgba(148,163,184,0.65)', size=5),
    name='Measured FRF (excited lines)',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |H| = %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>',
))
fig2.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=np.abs(fit.eval(freq)), mode='lines',
    line=dict(color=GOLD, width=2.0, dash='dash'), name='ML fit',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |G_fit| = %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>',
))

fig2.update_layout(
    template='plotly_white', height=360,
    margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=20, b=55),
    font=dict(family='Outfit, Inter, sans-serif', size=12),
    legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='bottom', y=1.02, xanchor='right', x=1,
                bgcolor='rgba(255,255,255,0.9)', bordercolor='#DCE5F0', borderwidth=1),
    xaxis=dict(title='Frequency  [Hz]', type='log', gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)'),
    yaxis=dict(title='|G(f)|', type='log', gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)'),
)
fig2.show()
```
